conventions.convention: The spacetime metric is η = diag(-1,1,1,1), while the Clifford contraction uses h = -η. The charge-g vertex is igγᵃ; an electron has g = -e_n. The rational fermion line is i(slash(p)+μ)/(h(p,p)-μ²), used off shell with nonzero denominator.
Formal series are interpreted coefficientwise over C[[z]]. The photon +i0 symbol denotes a boundary-value convention and supplies no multiplication rule for singular loop distributions.

The adopted regulator has finite nonempty vertex and link sets, s ≥ 1 matter modes per vertex, and fixed integer backgrounds 0 ≤ b_x ≤ s. It adds no spatial embedding or lattice spacing. Electric and CAR operators are dimensionless; Hamiltonian coefficients have units joules.
The regulator dynamics assume full AC and use U(t) = exp(-itH/ℏ), with t in seconds, on the exact Hamiltonian domain D(H₀).

Regional boundary flux has sign +1 on outgoing links and -1 on incoming links. The charged-insertion conclusion requires physical-sector preservation, preservation of every boundary electric domain, and commutation on those domains.

The infrared family uses the second-variable-linear Fock pairing, Lebesgue momentum measure d³k, a unit vector e, real λ ≠ 0, and 0 < ε < κ. Its profile is λ 1_{ε<|k|<κ}|k|^(-3/2)P_T(k)e, with C_λ = 8πλ²/3.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt as one selected regulated physical model the finite oriented-graph data of def-qft-compact-lattice-gauge-data, with finite nonempty vertex and link sets, compact U(1) rotor variables on links, finite CAR matter at vertices, fixed integer background b_x ∈ {0,…,s}, and the displayed Gauss operators.

Under the adopted fixed finite-graph model and AC, the physical sector is nonzero, H restricted to D(H) ∩ H_phys is self-adjoint, and exp(-itH_phys/ℏ) is a strongly continuous unitary group with exact derivative domain D(H) ∩ H_phys.

Under the adopted finite-graph model and AC, physical expectations of bounded gauge-charge eigenoperators vanish at nonzero total charge; the stated domain-qualified infinitesimal and time-ordered contact identities hold. A bounded physical-sector-preserving operator preserving and commuting with every boundary electric operator has zero regional-charge commutator on D_R. A separate continuum implication assumes the explicitly displayed common-domain, Gauss, locality and convergence hypotheses.

Adopt the stated finite/formal QED vertex and free-line convention, with coefficientwise finite-matrix inverses, explicit off-shell denominators, and an optional Countable-Choice-dependent free time-ordered distribution. No convergence, loop-product construction, continuum scattering operator or nonperturbative QED existence is asserted.

concerns.concern: Facts & Assumptions [F3] restates lem-qft-lattice-physical-evolution as saying that the restricted group 'has self-adjoint generator on D(H)∩H_phys'. The supplier's Statement and step 4.1 explicitly distinguish the skew-adjoint infinitesimal generator -iH_phys/ℏ from the self-adjoint Stone operator -H_phys/ℏ and the self-adjoint Hamiltonian H_phys. Specify which operator [F3] means. The theorem's own Statement and final proof step correctly assert self-adjointness of the restricted Hamiltonian.

seams_checked.note: The infrared example uses the adopted positive transverse free-photon Fock model and its exact energy multiplier domain. It retains Countable Choice, conditional draft status, and the exclusion of interacting charged-sector and empirical conclusions.

The finite graph, background range, exact domains, Gauss signs, selection/contact hypotheses and separate continuum assumptions match their suppliers. One citation wording mismatch remains: pthm-qft-lattice-gauge-existence [F3] calls the restricted group's generator self-adjoint, whereas lem-qft-lattice-physical-evolution distinguishes its skew-adjoint infinitesimal generator from its self-adjoint Stone operator and Hamiltonian. See the presentation concern.

The formal theorem retains invertible K₀, covariance of both coefficients, coefficientwise differentiation and finite on-shell current contractions. The infrared example verifies the nonzero transverse angular-profile hypothesis and proves its stronger phase-independent nonconvergence claim locally. Neither consumer adds loop, convergence or continuum-QED conclusions.

The observable-map postulate and scattering deduction preserve the charge-dependent vertex, photon numerator sign, off-shell fermion restriction and optional distributional qualification. The pair-production use evaluates the photon denominator at s > 0 and uses no internal fermion line. The downstream reading remains a selected leading formal coefficient, with no exact scattering operator or empirical error budget inferred.
